claims.claim: The patent for insulin was sold to the University of Toronto for one dollar.
claims.episode_span: A century after insulin's patent sold for a dollar, US vials listed for hundreds of dollars until public pressure forced 70–78% list-price cuts in 2023–24
claims.supporting_quote: The patent for insulin was sold to the University of Toronto for one dollar.

claims.claim: Human insulin is a protein of 51 amino acids with a molecular mass of 5808 Da.
claims.episode_span: The insulin molecule itself is a 51-amino-acid peptide whose constituent amino acids, at bulk commodity prices, amount to well under a dollar per gram.
claims.supporting_quote: A single protein (monomer) of human insulin is composed of 51 amino acids , and has a molecular mass of 5808

claims.claim: Recombinant insulin is produced in yeast (usually Saccharomyces cerevisiae) or E. coli.
claims.episode_span: Insulin manufacturing begins with engineered E. coli or yeast strains that express the protein in large bioreactors, followed by purification, formulation, and filling into vials or cartridges.
claims.supporting_quote: Recombinant insulin is produced either in yeast (usually Saccharomyces cerevisiae ) or E. coli

claims.claim: Three companies (Eli Lilly, Novo Nordisk, Sanofi) control over 90% of the global insulin market.
claims.episode_span: The result is a market in which three originator companies have maintained dominant share for decades, with limited entry by competitors.
claims.source_title: Lilly, Novo Nordisk and Sanofi slash prices of insulin in the US - GaBI Online
claims.supporting_quote: The three companies control over 90% of the global insulin market.

claims.claim: The US list price of a vial of Humalog rose from $21 in 1999 to $332 about twenty years later.
claims.episode_span: Against a U.S. list price that has ranged from one hundred to three hundred dollars or more in recent years
claims.source_title: After decades of profiteering, insulin manufacturer finally cuts the price - Lown Institute
claims.supporting_quote: In 1999, a vial of Humalog cost $21. Just twenty years later, the same vial costs $332

claims.claim: Estimated manufacturing cost of insulin therapy is about $61 per year for human insulin NPH and $111 per year for basal-bolus analog treatment - far below market prices.
claims.episode_span: That places the magic-wand floor somewhere between roughly three and eight dollars per vial under current technology, with the exact figure sensitive to volume and facility utilization.
claims.source_title: Diabetes Medication Can Be Manufactured at Lower Cost, New Study Says - Yale School of Medicine
claims.supporting_quote: Her findings include a manufacturing cost of $61 per year for twice-daily mixed human insulin NPH and $111 per year for basal-bolus treatment with insulin glargine and aspart.
